title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CARLA'S FERRY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Carla Benson, a deckhand on the ferry from Tacoma to Vashon Island, Washington.
Carla had not spoken to her big sister June in eleven years, all over their dad's old fishing boat, the Lucky Lou.
The funny part? June rode Carla's ferry every Thursday. And Carla hid behind the life jacket bin.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SHARP TONGUE
segments.quote: A sharp tongue is the only edge tool that grows keener with constant use.
segments.author: Washington Irving
lines: One morning in the galley, Carla told the crew the boat story. Again.
Old Captain Hank looked up from his Washington Irving paperback and read:
A sharp tongue is the only edge tool that grows keener with constant use.
Eleven years of sharpening. So she stopped telling the story.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE OTHER SIDE
segments.quote: If we could read the secret history of our enemies, we should find in each man's life sorrow and suffering enough to disarm all hostility.
segments.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
lines: At a wedding, cousin Dee let something slip.
June sold the boat the year her diner closed, to keep her house. Carla had never asked.
She thought of a line in her dad's old Longfellow book:
If we could read the secret history of our enemies, we should find in each man's life sorrow and suffering enough to disarm all hostility.
Her anger got a whole lot smaller.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TWO COFFEES
segments.quote: I would always rather be happy than dignified.
segments.author: Charlotte Brontë
lines: Thursday, Carla carried two coffees toward June's car, practicing a calm speech.
Then she slipped on the wet deck and landed flat on her backside.
She thought of Jane Eyre, the book she reads every winter:
I would always rather be happy than dignified.
So she sat in the puddle and laughed. June rolled down her window.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SPEECH
segments.quote: There is no revenge so complete as forgiveness.
segments.author: Josh Billings
lines: June said, I'm sorry about the boat.
For eleven years, Carla had practiced a speech in the shower to make June feel terrible.
Then she remembered the humorist Josh Billings:
There is no revenge so complete as forgiveness.
She said, I forgive you. And I'm sorry too.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TOAST
segments.quote: Comedy is simply a funny way of being serious.
segments.author: Peter Ustinov
lines: At Thanksgiving, everybody tiptoed. Uncle Ray even hid the fishing calendar.
Carla remembered the actor Peter Ustinov:
Comedy is simply a funny way of being serious.
She raised her glass. To the Lucky Lou, the most expensive silence in Washington State.
The table roared. They talked about Dad until midnight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE WATER
segments.quote: If there is magic on this planet, it is contained in water.
segments.author: Loren Eiseley
lines: In spring, they found the Lucky Lou in a Gig Harbor boatyard and split the nine hundred dollars.
They scraped and painted all April.
At sunrise, June took the wheel, and Carla read the writer Loren Eiseley:
If there is magic on this planet, it is contained in water.
Now they ride the ferry together. No more hiding.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dull the sharp tongue. Ask why. Laugh at yourself. Forgive. Joke about it. Go back to the water.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dull the sharp tongue. Ask why. Laugh at yourself. Forgive. Joke about it. Go back to the water.
My brother and I fought six years over a lawn mower. He kept it. It doesn't start.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
